Slide 1: Closing the Eastern County Touring Gap
Kettle Lane Youth Theatre | Ambry Falls
A proposal to the Tamsin Reade Fund for Rural Arts
Request: $45,000 to launch a second touring company in eastern Ambry County
Company start: January 2027

Slide 2: Eastern County Schools Are Asking. We Have Had to Say No.
In FY2026 we turned down 11 performance requests from eastern county schools
Four of the five eastern county schools we visit have no arts teacher on staff beyond music (Ambry County 2025 survey)
The drive runs up to 70 minutes each way
The reason we said no: one van and one touring cast

Slide 3: What Schools Already Get from Us
The Weathervane: a 40-minute, three-actor show about a girl who stops speaking after her family moves
Each show is followed by a 20-minute workshop led by the actors
FY2026: 31 performances in 14 schools
6,820 students reached in grades 3 through 8
Five of those 14 schools are in the eastern half of the county

Slide 4: The Plan: A Second Touring Company for the East
A touring company just for eastern county schools, starting with the spring 2027 semester
20 additional school visits in eastern Ambry County
An estimated 3,400 more students reached (estimate)
A follow-up workshop at every school
A new companion show for grades 6 through 8, alongside The Weathervane
An outside evaluation partner built into the budget

Slide 5: What Our FY2026 Results Show, and What They Don't
After-school student survey: "I feel confident speaking in front of my class at school"
September: 41 percent agreed. May: 74 percent agreed.
Limits: the answers are self-reported and there is no comparison group
We cannot say how much of the change came from us and how much from a year of growing up
Only 97 of 142 students completed both surveys; students who left may differ from those who stayed
A firmer measure: 83 percent of eligible students re-enrolled (98 of 118)
Waitlist for the 13-to-17 ensemble: 19 names in August

Slide 6: In a Student's Words
"I used to eat lunch in the library so nobody would talk to me. Now I'm the one who shows the new kids where the stage door is."
Wren, age 13, at the end-of-year circle, May 2026

Slide 7: The Ask: $45,000
Eastern County touring company budget: $68,500
Two touring teaching artists (school year): $44,000
Second van lease and fuel: $9,600
Production for the new companion show: $8,900
Outside evaluation partner: $6,000
Already in hand: $23,500
Projected touring fees from new schools (sliding scale, about $600 per visit): $12,000
Ambry County Arts Council rural access fund (approved September 2026): $11,500
Remaining gap: $45,000
We are asking the Tamsin Reade Fund to close that gap so the company can start in January 2027

Slide 8: A Well-Run Organization Ready to Grow
FY2026 expenses: $412,600. Revenue: $416,200. Operating surplus: $3,600 added to our cash reserve
About 81 percent of spending went to programs
61 percent of after-school students (87 of 142) received full or partial tuition aid; no student was turned away for cost
Support from 312 individual donors, the Halvorsen Family Foundation, and the Ambry County Arts Council
FY2027 evaluation: an outside evaluator, teacher ratings at two partner schools, and tracking of students who do not finish the year

P12.text:
## FY2026 Annual Program Report
### July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 | Ambry Falls
Kettle Lane Youth Theatre teaches young people ages 9 to 17 to make plays: acting, writing, building sets, running lights, and standing in front of a room without apologizing for being there. We work out of the second floor of the old Granary building on Kettle Lane, plus two school partner sites, and we take a small touring show into classrooms across Ambry County.
This report covers our fiscal year 2026. It is written for our board, our families, and the funders who carried us through it.

P13.text:
- **142 students** enrolled in the after-school company across three sites: the Granary (78), Brindle Elementary (36), and Ashgrove Middle School (28).
- **61 percent** of after-school students (87 of 142) received full or partial tuition aid. No student was turned away for cost.
- **48 students** attended the four-week summer intensive, up from 39 in FY2025.
- **3 mainstage productions** with **11 public performances** and **2,410 tickets** sold or given away.
- **31 touring performances** of our school-day show, *The Weathervane*, in **14 schools**, reaching **6,820 students** in grades 3 through 8.
- **83 percent** of eligible students returned from FY2025 (98 of 118 who had not aged out).
- **5 staff** (3 full-time, 2 part-time) and **14 teaching artists** on contract.

P14.text:
The core of the work. Students meet twice a week for 30 weeks, in mixed-age ensembles of 12 to 16. Each ensemble builds one short original piece in the fall and joins a mainstage production in the spring. Older students rotate through crew roles, and every student spends at least one production backstage. We believe a kid who has run a light board understands a play differently from one who has only stood in it.
This year the Brindle Elementary site moved from one day a week to two, at the school's request. Ashgrove Middle School was new in FY2026 and filled its 28 seats by the second week of October.

P15.text:
- *The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter* (November): an adaptation written with our 13-to-17 ensemble. 4 performances, 862 tickets.
- *Twelfth Night, Shortened* (March): 70 minutes, cast of 22. 4 performances, 931 tickets.
- *Small Town, Big Weather* (May): devised by students from interviews with Ambry Falls residents about the 1998 flood. 3 performances, 617 tickets.
About one ticket in five was given free to families through the Ambry Falls Public Library pass program.

P16.text:
A 40-minute, three-actor show about a girl who stops speaking after her family moves, followed by a 20-minute workshop led by the actors. We performed it 31 times this year in 14 schools. Nine of those schools are in Ambry Falls proper. Five are in the eastern half of the county, where the drive runs up to 70 minutes each way and where, according to the county's own 2025 survey, four of the five schools have no arts teacher on staff beyond music.
Demand outran us. We turned down 11 performance requests from eastern county schools because we had one van and one touring cast.

P17.text: Four weeks, five days a week, 48 students, ending in a showcase of scenes and original monologues. Tuition was $640, with aid available on the same scale as the after-school program.

P18.text:
We asked after-school students to answer the same short survey in September and again in May. One question asked whether they agreed with the statement "I feel confident speaking in front of my class at school."
**In September, 41 percent agreed. In May, 74 percent agreed.**
We are proud of that number, and we want to be plain about its limits. It is self-reported. We have no comparison group, so we cannot say how much of the change came from us and how much came from a year of growing up. And only 97 of 142 students completed both surveys; the students who left mid-year or missed survey days may not look like the ones who stayed. In FY2027 we plan to work with an outside evaluator, add a short teacher rating at two partner schools, and track students who do not finish the year.

P19.text:
What we can say with more confidence is that students keep coming back. 83 percent of eligible students re-enrolled, and the waitlist for the 13-to-17 ensemble reached 19 names in August.
One of those students, Wren, age 13, said this at the end-of-year circle in May:
> "I used to eat lunch in the library so nobody would talk to me. Now I'm the one who shows the new kids where the stage door is."

P20.text: Total FY2026 expenses were **$412,600**. Total revenue was **$416,200**, leaving a small operating surplus of **$3,600**, which goes to our cash reserve (now equal to about seven weeks of operating costs).

P21.text:
| Category | Amount |
|---|---|
| Program staff and teaching artists | $221,400 |
| Production (sets, costumes, scripts and rights) | $58,300 |
| Facility rent, Granary building | $46,800 |
| Administration | $38,700 |
| Touring (van lease, fuel, substitute coverage) | $24,900 |
| Fundraising | $22,500 |
| **Total** | **$412,600** |
Program costs (staff, production, touring, and the share of rent used for classes) came to about 81 percent of spending.

P22.text:
| Source | Amount | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Tuition and ticket sales | $131,200 | 32% |
| Individual donors and spring benefit (312 donors) | $118,400 | 28% |
| Halvorsen Family Foundation, general operating | $80,000 | 19% |
| Ambry County Arts Council, operating grant | $45,000 | 11% |
| School touring fees (14 schools) | $41,600 | 10% |
| **Total** | **$416,200** | **100%** |
Tuition covers less than a third of what we spend, by design. Our aid policy means families pay what they can, and the gap is closed by donors and grants. The Halvorsen grant is in year two of a three-year commitment.

P23.text:
Our biggest unmet need is the eastern half of the county. In FY2027 we will add a second touring company dedicated to those schools, so that *The Weathervane* and a new companion show for grades 6 through 8 can reach schools we currently turn away.
**Goal:** 20 additional school visits in eastern Ambry County, reaching an estimated 3,400 more students, with a follow-up workshop at each school.
**Cost: $68,500**
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Two touring teaching artists (school year) | $44,000 |
| Second van lease and fuel | $9,600 |
| Production for the new companion show | $8,900 |
| Outside evaluation partner | $6,000 |
| **Total** | **$68,500** |
**Committed or projected so far: $23,500.** That is $12,000 in touring fees from the new schools (charged on a sliding scale, $600 per visit on average) and $11,500 from the Ambry County Arts Council's rural access fund, approved in September.
P23.locator: “FY2027 plan: an Eastern County touring company”

P24.text: **Remaining gap: $45,000.** We are seeking that amount from a single funder so the company can start in January 2027, at the beginning of the spring semester.
P24.locator: “FY2027 plan: an Eastern County touring company”

P25.text:
To our families, our 312 donors, the Halvorsen Family Foundation, the Ambry County Arts Council, and the principals and teachers at 14 schools who cleared their gyms and cafeterias for us: this year happened because you made room.
Kettle Lane Youth Theatre | The Granary, 2nd Floor | Ambry Falls

P2.text:
KETTLE LANE YOUTH THEATRE
Board meeting notes, October 21, 2026
Present: Owen Calloway (chair), Dela Marchetti (executive director), Priya Haldane (treasurer), Teo Brask (development), Hannah Voss (board)

P4.text: Teo reported that Ruth Ellingsen, program officer at the Tamsin Reade Fund for Rural Arts, invited us to send a short deck before their December committee meeting. She asked specifically about the eastern county touring gap.

P5.text: Owen asked for a deck that requests $45,000 from the Reade Fund to close the gap on the $68,500 Eastern County touring company. Priya confirmed the $23,500 already in hand: $12,000 projected touring fees and $11,500 from the County Arts Council rural access fund.

P6.text: Deadline: draft to Owen and Dela by November 13. Final goes to Ruth Ellingsen by November 20, 2026.

P8.text:
1. Lead with the eastern county schools, not with our history. The 11 requests we turned down and the four of five schools with no arts teacher beyond music should be up front.
2. Use only FY2026 results from the annual report. The 3,400 additional students is an estimate and must be labeled as one.
3. Keep the caveat on the confidence survey (41 to 74 percent). Hannah: "If we drop the caveat, Ruth will find it in the report and we lose her trust." Do not present it as proof we caused the change.
4. No student photos and no last names. Wren's quote may be used with first name and age only; consent is on file.
5. Eight slides or fewer. The ask gets its own slide with the full $68,500 budget and the $45,000 gap stated plainly.

P9.text: Dela will send Teo the report file and brand sheet this week.
